name_en: UPI collect request ('enter PIN to receive money')
summary: The fraudster, often posing as a buyer, refund desk or cashback provider, sends a UPI 'collect' (request money) and tells the victim to approve it and enter the UPI PIN to receive money; approving actually debits the victim. NPCI's circular dated 29 July 2025 (as reported) stops person-to-person collect requests from 1 October 2025, but merchant collect requests continue, so payment requests that need a PIN still reach users.
victim_profile: general public; no specific profile documented
indicators: a payment request appears in the UPI app while someone on the phone says you are receiving money
you are asked to enter your UPI PIN to get a refund, cashback, prize or buyer payment
the request screen shows 'pay' or a debit amount, not a credit
the requester is a stranger, a marketplace buyer or a 'customer care' caller
pressure to approve quickly before the request 'expires'
typical_claims: I have sent you a request, just approve it and the money will come to you
enter your UPI PIN to receive the refund
approve the request to claim your cashback
this is how our payment system sends money to sellers
coaching_phrases: approve the request and enter your UPI PIN to receive the money
red_flag_questions: Did someone tell you that approving this request would put money into your account?
Is the person who sent this request someone you are buying from or selling to online?
Is anyone on the phone with you right now telling you what to tap?
Were you promised a refund, cashback or prize in return?
cues_en: they said i will receive money
i entered my pin and money went
cues_hinglish: paise receive karne ke liye pin
cashback ke liye request accept karo
maine pin daala aur paise kat gaye
jaldi accept karo expire ho jayegi
cues_hi: मैंने पिन डाला और पैसे कट गए

trend.note: Business Today (Aug 2025) reports NPCI's 29 July 2025 circular barring P2P collect from 1 Oct 2025 and says fraud had already dropped after the Rs 2,000 per-transaction P2P collect cap; merchant collect requests remain. Post-October 2025 reporting on enforcement was not found.

official_truth: You never need to enter your UPI PIN to receive money; the PIN is only ever used to send money out of your account.
advice: Decline any payment request from someone you do not know
Read the screen: if it asks for your PIN, money is leaving you
Report the requester's UPI ID in your app and on 1930 / cybercrime.gov.in
applicability_note: The victim authorises the debit by approving the request with their PIN, so Ruko can hold the payment and call before it settles.

summary: A fake buyer, frequently claiming to be an Army or paramilitary officer posted far away, agrees to buy something listed online, sends a fake payment screenshot and then a QR code, and guides the seller to scan it and enter the UPI PIN to 'receive' the money. Each scan debits the seller; the fraudster then sends a QR for double the amount to 'reverse the mistake', repeating until the victim stops.
victim_profile: Sellers advertising goods on online classified sites such as OLX and Quikr (Delhi Police).
indicators: buyer agrees to the price instantly without seeing the item
buyer claims to be in the Army or posted at a remote location and sends an ID card
buyer sends a QR code and asks you to scan it to receive payment
app asks for UPI PIN after scanning the buyer's code
after money is lost, buyer sends a new QR for a bigger amount to 'refund' it
fake payment screenshot instead of a real credit in the account
typical_claims: I am in the Army, posted far away, so I will pay online
scan this QR code and the payment will come to you
there was a technical issue, scan this one to get your money back
I sent double by mistake, scan again to fix it
coaching_phrases: scan this QR code and enter your UPI PIN to receive the payment
scan the new QR code to get your money refunded
red_flag_questions: Are you selling something online and is this payment linked to that buyer?
Did the buyer send you a QR code and ask you to scan it to get paid?
Has the buyer said they are in the Army or posted far away?
Have you already lost money and been told this payment will reverse it?
cues_hinglish: qr scan karo paise aa jayenge
refund ke liye dobara scan karo
paise aane ki jagah kat gaye
cues_hi: पैसे आने की जगह कट गए

trend.note: No official statistic found for this specific pattern.

official_truth: Scanning a QR code and entering your PIN always sends money out; nobody can pay you by asking you to scan their code.
advice: Never scan a QR code or enter a PIN to receive money
Ask the buyer to pay to your UPI ID and check your bank balance, not a screenshot
Stop after the first loss; a 'refund QR' is the same trick
Report on 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in
applicability_note: Each scan is a victim-authorised UPI debit to the fraudster, so Ruko can hold it, especially repeated escalating payments to the same payee.

summary: A caller posing as an event organiser or job interviewer says a mutual friend gave them the victim's number and asks the victim to merge in a call from the 'friend'. The second call is actually the bank's genuine OTP verification call triggered by the fraudster, so the fraudster hears the OTP and completes a transaction or account takeover.
victim_profile: general public; no specific profile documented
indicators: unknown caller says a friend gave them your number
caller asks you to merge or conference in another incoming call
an automated bank call or OTP call arrives during the conversation
you receive an OTP for a transaction you did not start
caller pretends to invite you to an event or a job interview
typical_claims: your friend gave me your number
my friend is calling from another number, please merge the call
I am calling about the event invitation
this is regarding your job interview
coaching_phrases: merge the incoming call with this one so we can all talk
red_flag_questions: Did anyone ask you to merge or add another call recently?
Did you get an OTP or a bank verification call that you did not ask for?
Has a stranger called saying a friend gave them your number?
Is this transaction one you started yourself?
cues_hinglish: dost ka call merge kar do

trend.note: NPCI flagged it as a new tactic in February 2025; no official volume figures found.

official_truth: Banks never ask for your OTP on a call, and you should never merge a call from an unknown number.
advice: Do not merge or conference calls from unknown numbers
Never read out or share an OTP with anyone
If an OTP arrives for something you did not start, call your bank and 1930 immediately
applicability_note: The fraudster uses the stolen OTP to move money themselves, so Ruko cannot hold a victim-initiated payment; it can only warn on its public line and flag the account.

name_en: SIM swap / eSIM activation / '5G SIM upgrade'
summary: Fraudsters posing as telecom operator staff call or text about a SIM upgrade, 5G upgrade, KYC or eSIM activation and get the victim to click a link, share an OTP or confirm a code. The victim's number moves to a SIM or eSIM controlled by the fraudster, the victim's phone loses signal, and bank OTPs and alerts go to the fraudster, who resets credentials and drains accounts.
victim_profile: I4C says users of all age groups are targeted (as reported by Digit, 2025); no narrower profile documented.
indicators: call or SMS offering a free 4G-to-5G SIM upgrade or eSIM activation
link or code to 'activate eSIM' that you did not request
phone suddenly shows no signal or 'SIM not registered'
OTPs and bank SMS stop arriving
caller claims to be from Jio, Airtel, Vi or BSNL and asks for an OTP
typical_claims: your SIM will be blocked today unless you upgrade
we will upgrade your SIM to 5G free, just share the OTP
click this link to activate your eSIM
your KYC for the SIM is pending
coaching_phrases: click the link to activate your eSIM
share the OTP to complete the 5G upgrade
red_flag_questions: Has your mobile signal or SIM stopped working in the last day or two?
Did anyone call you about a SIM upgrade, 5G or eSIM?
Did you click a link or share a code about your SIM?
Are you receiving your bank SMS alerts normally?

first_seen.value: 5G-upgrade variant by October 2022; eSIM variant reported 2025

trend.note: I4C issued a public warning on eSIM fraud in 2025 (Digit, BOOM); no official volume figure for eSIM fraud found.

official_truth: Telecom companies do not need your OTP or a link click to upgrade your SIM or activate an eSIM; do it only at the operator's store or official app.
advice: Never click SIM upgrade or eSIM links from calls or SMS
If your signal suddenly vanishes, call your operator and bank to freeze the SIM and accounts
Report to 1930 and cybercrime.gov.in
applicability_note: The fraudster moves money using the hijacked number, so there is no victim-initiated payment for Ruko to hold; Ruko can only warn and alert the bank.

summary: A victim waiting for a refund (failed payment, cancelled order, overcharge) or lured by a 'cashback' or reward is contacted by, or calls, a fake customer care agent often found through a search engine. The agent tells them to scan a QR code, approve a request, enter their UPI PIN, pay a small 'verification' amount or install an app 'to process the refund', which instead sends money out or hands over the account.
victim_profile: Customers seeking refunds from food delivery, airline and travel platforms who searched online for helpline numbers (Hyderabad police cases, 2020); otherwise general public.
indicators: customer care number found through a Google or Justdial search rather than the official app
agent asks for UPI PIN, OTP or card details to issue a refund
refund requires scanning a QR code or approving a payment request
asked to pay a small token amount (e.g. Rs 5-100) to 'verify' the account
asked to install a remote-access or support app
typical_claims: your refund is approved, scan this to receive it
enter your UPI PIN to get the refund credited
pay Rs 10 to verify your account and the refund will come
you have won cashback, approve the request to claim it
coaching_phrases: scan this code and enter your PIN to get your refund
approve the pending request to release your refund or cashback
install this app so we can process your refund
red_flag_questions: Is this payment connected to getting a refund or cashback?
Where did you find the customer care number you called?
Did the agent ask you to scan a code, approve a request or enter your PIN?
Has anyone asked you to pay a small amount first to verify your account?
cues_hi: वेरिफाई के लिए दस रुपये भेजो

trend.note: Still described as a current UPI trick in August 2026 (Moneylife); no official volume figures found.

official_truth: A refund or cashback never needs your UPI PIN, OTP, a QR scan or a payment from you; genuine customer care will not ask for them.
advice: Use the helpline inside the official app or website, never a searched number
Refuse any request to scan, approve, pay or enter a PIN to get a refund
Report on 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in
applicability_note: Most variants need the victim to authorise a UPI debit (QR scan, request approval or token payment), which Ruko can hold; the remote-access variant overlaps with remote_access.

name_en: 'Sent by mistake, please return' with fake credit SMS
summary: A caller posing as a relative's friend or acquaintance says he owes or is sending money to the family and will transfer it to the victim. While on the line he sends fake 'credited' SMSes from an ordinary mobile number, then claims he sent too much by mistake (e.g. 30,000 instead of 3,000) and urgently asks for the difference back, often citing a hospital emergency; no money ever arrived.
victim_profile: general public; no specific profile documented
indicators: unknown caller claims to know your father or another relative
credit alert SMS comes from a 10-digit mobile number, not the bank's sender ID
caller says he sent extra by mistake and asks for the excess back
bank app balance does not show the credit
caller stays on the line, pushes urgency or a medical emergency
refund to be sent to a different UPI ID or number than the sender
typical_claims: I am your father's friend, he asked me to send money to you
I sent 30,000 instead of 3,000 by mistake, please return the rest
check your SMS, the money has come
I am at the hospital, please send it back quickly
coaching_phrases: return the extra money immediately, I am at the hospital
check your SMS inbox to verify the credit and send back the excess
send the return to this other UPI ID
red_flag_questions: Did someone tell you they sent you money by mistake and ask for it back?
Have you checked your bank app balance, not just an SMS, to see if the money actually arrived?
Did the credit message come from a normal mobile number?
Is the person asking for the return someone you know personally, and have you called your relative to check?
cues_hinglish: papa ke dost bol raha hoon
sms check karo paise aa gaye
cues_hi: पापा का दोस्त बोल रहा हूँ
मैसेज चेक करो पैसे आ गए
तीन हजार की जगह तीस हजार

trend.note: Cases reported in 2024, 2025 and September 2026 (Outlook Money, The Quint, Free Press Journal); no official statistics found.

official_truth: An SMS is not proof of money received; genuine bank alerts come from the bank's sender ID, so check your balance in the bank app and never 'return' money to a stranger.
advice: Check the balance in your bank app before sending anything back
Call the relative the caller named on a number you already have
If money really arrived by mistake, let the bank reverse it rather than paying a stranger
Report on 1930, cybercrime.gov.in or Chakshu
applicability_note: The victim pushes the 'return' payment themselves, so Ruko can hold it; no official (government/regulator) source for this pattern was found, only news.

summary: A fake bank, wallet, telecom or company 'customer care' agent (often reached via a searched helpline number) tells the victim to install a screen-sharing or remote-control app such as AnyDesk, TeamViewer or QuickSupport and read out the access code. The fraudster then watches or controls the phone, sees OTPs and PINs as they are typed, and makes transactions through the victim's own banking and UPI apps.
victim_profile: general public; customers seeking help for a refund, KYC, blocked account or failed transaction (RBI, Hyderabad police); no narrower profile documented.
indicators: agent asks you to install AnyDesk, TeamViewer, QuickSupport or another 'support' app
asked to read out a 9-digit or similar access code
asked to open your bank or UPI app while the call or screen share is on
phone shows a screen-sharing or recording icon
helpline number was found through a search engine or social media
typical_claims: install this app so I can fix your problem
tell me the code shown on your screen
we need access to your phone to process your refund or KYC
coaching_phrases: install this support app and read out the code shown on your screen
install this remote access app so we can fix your payment problem
red_flag_questions: Did anyone ask you to install an app or share your screen today?
Is someone on a call guiding you through this payment right now?
Did you get this helpline number from a search engine or social media?
Is a screen-sharing or remote app installed on this phone?
cues_hinglish: app install karo problem theek ho jayegi
code batao jo screen pe hai
phone pe app daalne ko bola
wo meri screen dekh raha tha
cues_hi: स्क्रीन पर जो कोड है बताओ
वो मेरी स्क्रीन देख रहा था

trend.note: RBI listed remote-access apps among common frauds again in January 2022; in November 2025 Google piloted screen-sharing warnings with Indian payment apps (Storyboard18). No official volume figures found for this pattern.

official_truth: No genuine bank, NPCI or company support agent will ask you to install a screen-sharing app or give them access to your phone.
advice: Hang up and uninstall any app a caller asked you to install
Never open banking apps while sharing your screen
Call your bank on the number printed on your card and 1930 if access was given
applicability_note: Transactions are made on the victim's own device and app, so Ruko can hold them if flagged, but the victim may not realise a payment is being made by the fraudster.

name_en: Malicious APK on WhatsApp (wedding invite, bank, PM-Kisan, e-challan)
summary: Victims receive an .apk file or link on WhatsApp, SMS or Telegram disguised as a wedding invitation, bank KYC/rewards app, PM-Kisan scheme app, RTO e-challan or gas bill update. Installing it gives the malware access to SMS, contacts and banking data; it reads and forwards bank OTPs, overlays fake banking screens and often forwards itself to the victim's contacts, after which money is debited to mule accounts.
victim_profile: general public; wedding-season recipients (Himachal police), PM-Kisan-themed lures suggest farmers and scheme beneficiaries but no profile is stated by sources.
indicators: a file ending in .apk sent on WhatsApp or Telegram
wedding card, challan, PM-Kisan or bank update sent as an app rather than a PDF or image
message from an unknown number or a contact's hacked account
app asks for SMS, call, contacts, accessibility or VPN permissions
phone overheats, restarts or sends messages to contacts by itself
OTP SMSes you did not see, followed by debits
typical_claims: you are invited to our wedding, open the card
your traffic challan is pending, download the app to pay
your PM Kisan instalment is pending, install the app
your bank KYC or reward points will expire, update via this app
your gas connection will be cut, update the bill
coaching_phrases: install the update to complete the process
red_flag_questions: Did you install any app from a WhatsApp file or link in the last few days?
Was it a wedding card, challan, PM-Kisan or bank app sent as a file?
Has your phone been sending messages to your contacts on its own?
Are you seeing OTPs or transactions that you did not start?
cues_hinglish: app install kiya aur paise kat gaye
cues_hi: ऐप इंस्टॉल किया और पैसे कट गए

first_seen.value: unknown (cases in sources reviewed date from July 2025)

trend.note: Surat Cyber Crime Cell linked 336 APKs to about Rs 125.39 crore of debits across 1,06,643 transactions (IANS, Aug 2026); CERT-In alerted on an e-challan/gas-bill APK campaign (Moneylife, Mar 2026).

official_truth: Genuine wedding cards come as images or PDFs and banks, PM-Kisan and e-challan services never send apps as APK files on WhatsApp; install apps only from the official app store.
advice: Never open .apk files from WhatsApp, SMS or Telegram
If installed, disconnect data, uninstall, and change UPI PIN and banking passwords from a clean device
Call your bank and 1930 immediately to block debits
applicability_note: Money is moved by the attacker using intercepted OTPs, not by the victim, so Ruko can only warn and alert the bank; a sudden unusual debit could still be flagged.

name_en: Task-based part-time job scam (like, review, rate)
summary: An ad or WhatsApp message offers easy work-from-home income for liking videos, subscribing to channels, or rating restaurants, hotels or map locations. After small genuine payouts, the victim is moved to a Telegram 'VIP' group and told to prepay for higher-paying tasks; the balance shown on a fake site grows but withdrawals are blocked until the victim pays for 'task errors', a low 'credit score', taxes or account upgrades, until the money is gone.
victim_profile: Retired employees, women and unemployed youth looking for part-time work (MHA/I4C as reported by The News Minute, 2023).
indicators: unsolicited offer of Rs 500-1,000+ a day for liking videos or giving reviews
moved from WhatsApp to a Telegram 'VIP' or 'task' group
small first payouts, then a request to deposit money to unlock bigger tasks
balance shown on a website or app but withdrawal blocked
asked to pay for 'task errors', 'credit score', tax or account upgrade before withdrawing
payments go to different personal bank accounts or UPI IDs each time
typical_claims: earn from home just by liking YouTube videos
rate restaurants and get commission daily
this is a prepaid task, deposit to get higher returns
you made a mistake in the task, pay to repair it
your credit score is low, pay to restore it before withdrawal
coaching_phrases: pay the task repair amount to unlock your withdrawal
your credit score is low, pay this to release the money
red_flag_questions: Is this payment to unlock earnings from online tasks such as likes, reviews or ratings?
Did you get this work through WhatsApp or Telegram from someone you have never met?
Have you been able to withdraw your full balance, or are you being asked to pay first?
Are you sending money to a different person's account each time?
cues_hinglish: paise nikalne ke liye aur bharna padega
cues_hi: पैसे निकालने के लिए और भरना होगा

trend.note: MHA had 100+ task-fraud websites blocked in December 2023; large individual losses still reported in 2025 (Cyberabad, Rs 32.8 lakh). No official trend figure for this pattern alone was verified.

official_truth: No genuine job asks you to pay money to earn, and a website balance you must pay to withdraw is not real money.
advice: Stop paying; every 'unlock' fee is followed by another
Never deposit money to get paid for online tasks
Report the Telegram/WhatsApp accounts and payee accounts on 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in
applicability_note: Victims push repeated UPI/IMPS transfers to changing personal accounts, which Ruko can hold and question.

name_en: Fake job offer with fees (incl. overseas 'cyber slavery' recruitment)
summary: Fraudsters harvest job-seeker details from job portals or advertise government, airline, IT or overseas jobs, hold fake interviews and send fake offer or selection letters, then collect staged fees for registration, insurance, security deposit, training or visa processing until the victim stops paying. An overseas variant uses fake job offers from dubious firms and unscrupulous agents to send Indians to scam compounds in Cambodia, Laos and Myanmar, where they are forced into cyber fraud ('cyber slavery').
victim_profile: Job seekers, including highly educated engineers, MBA, MCA and pharma graduates (Hyderabad police, 2025); unemployed youth and students lured abroad (CRPF Cyber Byte citing MHA, 2025).
indicators: offer arrives without a proper application or after a very short interview
payment demanded for registration, insurance, security deposit, training, uniform or offer letter
each payment is followed by a new fee or a 'payment gateway stuck' excuse
offer letter or appointment from a government body or airline sent on WhatsApp or Gmail
overseas job through a private agent, especially to Cambodia, Laos or Myanmar
fees go to personal bank accounts or UPI IDs
typical_claims: you are selected, pay the registration fee to receive your offer letter
pay a refundable security deposit to confirm your joining
training and uniform charges are required before joining
well-paid job abroad, the agent will arrange travel
your visa and job abroad are approved, pay the processing fee
red_flag_questions: Is this payment a fee for a job, offer letter, training or visa?
How did you apply, and have you met the employer in person?
Is the job abroad, and is a private agent arranging your travel?
Have you been asked to pay more than once for the same job?

trend.note: Hyderabad police cite 26,809 fake job scam cases in Telangana from Jan 2024 to Aug 2025 (ETV Bharat); MEA told Parliament 6,998 Indians were rescued from scam compounds in Cambodia, Laos and Myanmar in 2022-2025 (Scroll, Feb 2026).

official_truth: Genuine employers and government recruiters such as India Post do not ask for money to give you a job; overseas jobs should only be taken through government-authorised recruiting agents.
advice: Do not pay any fee to get a job or an offer letter
Verify the employer on its official website and overseas recruiters with the Indian mission or eMigrate
Report on 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in
applicability_note: Victims pay staged fees by UPI or bank transfer to personal accounts, which Ruko can hold; the trafficking risk itself needs a warning, not just a payment hold.

name_en: Fake stock trading / WhatsApp investment group
summary: Victims are added to WhatsApp or Telegram 'stock tips' groups run by people posing as market experts or staff of reputed brokerages, sometimes showing fake SEBI certificates. They are told to install a trading app via a private link offering an 'institutional account', discounted IPOs or guaranteed allotment, and transfer money to various bank accounts; the app shows huge fake profits, and withdrawal is blocked or needs further 'tax', fee or verification payments.
victim_profile: Retired professionals and bank officials appear in reported cases (e.g. a retired Mumbai scientist, a Palghar bank official); no official target profile documented.
indicators: added to a WhatsApp or Telegram group sharing 'VIP' stock tips
trading app downloaded from a link, not the Play Store or App Store
offer of an institutional or FPI account, discounted IPO or guaranteed allotment
money sent to different individual or company bank accounts, not your own demat/broker account
app shows very large profits but withdrawal fails
asked to pay tax, fees or a percentage before withdrawal
typical_claims: join our VIP group for guaranteed daily profits
we will open an institutional account so you get IPO allotment
our firm is SEBI registered, here is the certificate
pay 10 percent tax to release your profit
deposit more to upgrade your account and unlock withdrawal
red_flag_questions: Is this money going into a trading or investment account someone on WhatsApp or Telegram told you about?
Did you download the trading app from a link someone sent you?
Have you been able to withdraw your profits to your own bank account?
Are you being asked to pay tax or a fee to release your profits?
cues_hinglish: app mein profit dikh raha hai
cues_hi: ऐप में प्रॉफिट दिख रहा है

trend.note: I4C (July 2026) and SEBI (August 2025) both issued fresh warnings; no verified national loss figure for this pattern alone.

official_truth: SEBI says there is no such thing as an 'institutional trading account' for resident Indians, and genuine brokers never ask for extra deposits or tax to release your own money.
advice: Invest only through SEBI-registered brokers' official apps and your own demat account
Check registration on sebi.gov.in before paying anyone
Never pay to withdraw profits; report on 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in
applicability_note: Victims push large NEFT/RTGS/IMPS transfers to third-party accounts themselves, which Ruko can hold and question.

name_en: Fake crypto / forex platform and 'pig butchering'
summary: Fraudsters build trust over days or weeks through chats, social media or task groups, then persuade the victim to invest in cryptocurrency, forex or another 'lucrative scheme' on a fake app or website guided by 'teachers' or mentors. The platform shows rising balances, but withdrawals are blocked and more payments are demanded until the victim stops; the government links such 'pig butchering' operations to scam compounds abroad.
victim_profile: Unemployed youth, students, housewives and needy people (government alert summarised by CRPF Cyber Byte, March 2025, citing the MHA annual report).
indicators: online contact who builds a friendship before talking about investing
crypto, bitcoin or forex trading on an app or site shared by link
a 'teacher', mentor or group admin guides each trade
balance grows quickly but withdrawal is blocked
asked to pay more to unlock, upgrade or verify the account
payments go to individual bank accounts or UPI IDs rather than a registered exchange
typical_claims: I made big profits trading crypto, let me teach you
this platform gives guaranteed daily returns
follow the teacher's signals in the group
your account needs a deposit before you can withdraw
red_flag_questions: Is this payment for crypto, bitcoin or forex trading on an app someone online introduced you to?
Have you met this person face to face?
Have you successfully withdrawn money from this platform to your own account?
Are you paying to unlock or upgrade your account?
cues_hinglish: account unlock karne ke liye paise
cues_hi: अकाउंट अनलॉक करने के लिए पैसे

first_seen.value: originated in China around 2016 (as stated in CRPF Cyber Byte, March 2025)

trend.note: Government alert in 2025 flagged pig-butchering targeting youth and housewives; no verified India-specific volume figure found. RBI's Alert List of unauthorised forex platforms could not be opened (rbi.org.in blocked automated access).

official_truth: The government warns that 'pig butchering' schemes build trust and then steal money put into crypto or other lucrative-looking schemes; no genuine platform makes you pay to withdraw your own money.
advice: Do not invest on apps or sites shared by online contacts
Never pay to unlock a withdrawal
Report on 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in and keep transaction IDs
applicability_note: Victims transfer money themselves, often repeatedly to changing accounts, which Ruko can hold.

name_en: Ponzi / unregulated deposit, chit or MLM scheme
summary: A company, 'chit fund' or network scheme collects deposits from the public through commission agents, relatives or community members, promising unusually high fixed returns or bonuses for recruiting others. Early investors are paid from later deposits until the scheme stops paying and collapses; such schemes are unregistered with any financial regulator, which is itself an offence under the BUDS Act, 2019.
victim_profile: Small depositors reached through local commission agents (Saradha case); no specific profile documented in official sources reviewed.
indicators: fixed returns far above bank deposit rates
money collected by agents who earn commission
bonus or higher return for bringing in new members
scheme is not registered with RBI, SEBI or another regulator
pressure to reinvest rather than withdraw
delays in paying returns explained as temporary
typical_claims: your money will double in a short time
guaranteed monthly return, better than any bank
bring two more members and earn extra commission
this is a registered chit fund, completely safe
red_flag_questions: Is this payment a deposit into a scheme promising a fixed high return?
Is the scheme registered with RBI, SEBI or another regulator, and have you checked?
Did an agent or acquaintance who earns commission bring you in?
Are you promised extra money for recruiting others?

trend.note: No recent official statistics verified in this run.

official_truth: Under the Banning of Unregulated Deposit Schemes Act, taking deposits through any scheme not registered with a financial regulator is a crime, so a promise of high fixed returns from such a scheme is not protected.
advice: Check that the entity is registered with RBI, SEBI or the relevant regulator before depositing
Avoid schemes that pay for recruiting members
Report unregistered deposit schemes to the police or the state competent authority
applicability_note: Deposits paid by bank transfer can be held, but many schemes collect cash through agents and the victim is often a willing, trusting payer.

name_en: Illegal instant loan app with extortion and recovery harassment
summary: Unauthorised instant loan apps, often installed via APK links outside the Play Store or disguised as finance tools, demand access to contacts, call logs, SMS, photos and location, then extort money through threats and harassment, including blackmail using data taken from the phone, with callers posing as company or recovery representatives. Police have linked such app networks to shell companies run for foreign operatives.
victim_profile: general public; no specific profile documented in sources reviewed.
indicators: loan app installed from a link or APK, not from a known bank or NBFC
app demanded access to contacts, photos, SMS and location
threatening calls or messages to you or your contacts
callers posing as the company or recovery agents demand immediate payment
payment demanded to a personal UPI ID or a new account each time
typical_claims: pay today or we will message everyone in your contacts
your photos will be sent to your family and friends
you have defaulted, pay the penalty immediately
red_flag_questions: Is this payment to repay a loan from an app?
Is the app's lender a bank or RBI-registered NBFC that you can name?
Is anyone threatening you or contacting your family about this loan?
Are you being asked to pay to a personal UPI ID?
cues_hinglish: loan app wale dhamki de rahe
loan app ne contacts le liye
cues_hi: लोन ऐप वाले धमकी दे रहे
लोन ऐप ने कॉन्टैक्ट्स ले लिए

trend.note: CRPF Cyber Byte reported a Rs 750 crore loan-app extortion network (Uttarakhand STF, July 2025) and SpyLend loan-app malware (March 2025); no national statistic verified in this run.

official_truth: RBI warns that illegal loan apps and fraudsters posing as recovery agents are a known fraud; borrow only from banks or RBI-regulated lenders and report threats to the police.
advice: Do not pay extortion demands to personal accounts; keep screenshots of threats
Report the app and threats on 1930, cybercrime.gov.in and to local police
Revoke the app's permissions and uninstall it; tell close contacts to ignore messages
applicability_note: Extortion repayments are victim-initiated UPI transfers that Ruko can hold, though the victim may insist on paying out of fear.

name_en: Fake loan approval with upfront fee
summary: Fraudsters advertise easy loans through fake websites, apps, calls or social media, sometimes using the name of a known lender or payment app, and tell the applicant the loan is approved. Before disbursal they demand upfront payments described as processing, insurance, GST or other charges, keep inventing new fees, and the loan never arrives.
victim_profile: Small borrowers seeking quick credit (e.g. a fruit vendor applying for a Rs 3 lakh loan, Indore police case 2026); otherwise general public.
indicators: loan approved without proper documents or credit check
asked to pay before receiving the loan
fees described as processing, insurance, GST, file charge or verification
lender uses a well-known brand name but contacts you on WhatsApp or a personal number
payment goes to a personal UPI ID or account
caller asks to take your phone or install an app to 'process' the loan
typical_claims: your loan is sanctioned, pay the processing fee to release it
insurance charge is mandatory before disbursal
pay GST on the loan amount first
one last charge and the money will be credited today
red_flag_questions: Is this payment a fee to receive a loan?
Which bank or NBFC approved the loan, and did you apply on its official website or branch?
Have you been asked to pay more than one charge before getting the money?
Is the fee going to a personal UPI ID?

trend.note: Only individual cases verified in this run (Indore, 2026); no official statistic found.

official_truth: RBI lists fake loan websites and apps among common frauds; a genuine regulated lender deducts any charges transparently and does not demand fees to a personal account before disbursal.
advice: Apply only through a bank or RBI-regulated NBFC's official website, app or branch
Never pay a fee to a personal account to release a loan
Do not hand your phone to anyone claiming to process your loan; report on 1930
applicability_note: Victims pay the fees themselves by UPI or transfer; weak sourcing: only one police case and RBI's general warning were verified in this run.

name_en: Renting or selling your bank account or SIM (money mule)
summary: Fraud networks pay people a commission or fee to hand over or 'rent' their bank accounts, debit cards, net-banking access or SIM cards, or to receive money and forward it. These mule accounts and SIMs are then used to receive and launder proceeds of investment, task, APK and other frauds; account holders who sell or rent them face arrest, and police have also arrested bank employees who helped open such accounts.
victim_profile: general public; no specific profile documented in sources reviewed (cases include account holders and bank staff).
indicators: offer of commission or monthly rent for using your bank account
asked to hand over debit card, passbook, cheque book, net-banking login or SIM
asked to open a new account or SIM in your name for someone else
money arrives from strangers and you are told to forward it
told to withdraw cash or send money onward and keep a percentage
typical_claims: sell or lend your account and earn a commission on every amount that passes through
money will come in, forward it to this account and keep your share
red_flag_questions: Has anyone asked to use your bank account, card or SIM in return for money?
Did you recently receive money from people you do not know and get asked to send it on?
Is this transfer forwarding money that came into your account from someone else?
Did someone help you open this account and keep the card or login?
cues_hinglish: sim card de do paise milenge

trend.note: Police and MHA describe mule/rented accounts as core to organised fraud (TNM 2023; IANS 2026 Surat case routing Rs 125 crore through mule accounts); Gurugram police said 33 bank employees had been arrested (2025). RBI's MuleHunter.AI could not be verified in this run.

official_truth: Letting criminals use your bank account or SIM makes you part of the fraud: DoT says obtaining SIMs for others' misuse is an offence under the Telecommunications Act, 2023, and police arrest account sellers.
advice: Never rent, sell or lend your account, card, login or SIM
If unknown money arrives, do not forward it; tell your bank
Report recruiters on 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in
applicability_note: Ruko can hold onward transfers from an account that suddenly receives and forwards stranger funds, but many mule accounts are fully controlled by the fraudsters.

name_en: Illegal betting / online money gaming app
summary: Illegal betting and online money-gaming apps lure users into depositing money into an in-app wallet with fake promises of large returns or winnings. The government says such apps have generated over Rs 400 crore of criminal proceeds (citing the ED), and the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025 bans online money gaming along with its promotion, advertising and payments.
victim_profile: general public; no specific profile documented in sources reviewed.
indicators: app installed from a link or APK, not an official store
deposit money into a game wallet to bet or 'predict'
each deposit goes to a different personal UPI ID or account
promises of doubling money or guaranteed winnings
withdrawal delayed, blocked or needing a further deposit
promoted by influencers or Telegram 'tipsters'
typical_claims: deposit and win double in minutes
guaranteed winning tips, join our Telegram
add more to your wallet to unlock withdrawal
everyone is winning, do not miss today's match
red_flag_questions: Is this payment to add money to a betting, gaming or prediction app wallet?
Was the app installed from a link rather than the Play Store?
Is the payee a different person each time you deposit?
Have you been able to withdraw your winnings to your own account?

trend.note: PIB (Oct 2025), citing the ED annual report 2024-25, says online betting apps generated over Rs 400 crore in criminal proceeds; the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act was passed on 21 Aug 2025, banning online money gaming. Post-ban trend not verified.

official_truth: Online money gaming, including its promotion, advertisements and payments, is banned in India under the 2025 online gaming law, so any app taking money for bets is illegal.
advice: Do not deposit money into betting or money-gaming apps
Uninstall APK-based gaming apps and revoke their permissions
Report the app and payee accounts on 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in
applicability_note: Wallet deposits are victim-initiated UPI transfers to personal/mule accounts, which Ruko can hold; sourcing in this run is thin (one PIB backgrounder).

name_en: Fake UPI payment screenshot / spoof payment app
summary: A buyer shows a shopkeeper or online seller a doctored payment screenshot or a spoof payment-app screen as 'proof' that money was sent, takes the goods, and leaves; no money reaches the account. In marketplace scams the fake screenshot is the opening move before the fraudster sends QR codes that debit the seller.
victim_profile: Shopkeepers and small merchants (Moneylife, 2026) and online classified sellers (Delhi Police).
indicators: customer shows a screenshot or their own phone screen instead of you receiving a credit alert
no sound-box or bank credit notification for the payment
customer is in a hurry and leaves quickly
buyer says payment is done but asks you to scan a QR to 'receive' it
typical_claims: payment done, see the screenshot
there was a technical issue, the money will come
I have paid, check your phone later
red_flag_questions: Did you see the credit in your own bank app or only a screenshot from the buyer?
Is the buyer now asking you to scan a QR code or approve something to receive the money?
Has the same buyer sent screenshots more than once?
cues_en: showed me payment on his phone

trend.note: Reported as a current tactic in August 2026 (Moneylife); no statistics found.

official_truth: A screenshot is not proof of payment; only a credit shown in your own bank or UPI app counts.
advice: Release goods only after the credit appears in your own bank app or sound box
Never scan a buyer's QR or enter a PIN to receive money
Report repeat offenders to local police or 1930
applicability_note: The victim loses goods rather than sending a payment, so Ruko can only warn; it becomes direct if the fraudster follows up with a QR or collect request.
